title: MCP Primitives and Lifecycle Reference
summary: A beginner reference and offline exercise for distinguishing MCP roles, primitives, capability claims, trusted host policy, and provider adapter boundaries.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with AI tools and client-server systems
Basic Python 3 knowledge for the offline exercise

sections.title: Map the roles, layers, and primitives
paragraphs: Model Context Protocol, or MCP, concerns context exchange rather than language-model orchestration. An MCP host is the AI application coordinating one or more MCP clients. Each client maintains a connection to an MCP server. A host decision, such as whether to approve a write, is not the same thing as a server capability or annotation.

The data layer uses JSON-RPC messages for lifecycle, capabilities, primitives, and notifications. A transport carries those messages. The documented transports are local standard input/output, called stdio, and remote Streamable HTTP. JSON-RPC is therefore not a transport, and choosing Streamable HTTP does not by itself establish authentication or authorization.

A server can expose tools, resources, and prompts. A tool is an executable function, such as searching a catalog or creating a record. A resource supplies contextual data, such as a document or status record. A prompt is a reusable interaction template. A data item is not automatically a resource, an executable operation is not a prompt, and none of these categories grants permission to use the primitive.

A client can offer elicitation, through which a server requests additional user input or confirmation. Elicitation is not silent approval. Notifications are opt-in through subscription or listen behavior. Sampling and logging are deprecated client primitives in protocol version 2026-07-28. The architecture documentation directs new implementations to use provider APIs directly for sampling and stderr or OpenTelemetry for logging.

The supplied architecture evidence describes version 2026-07-28 as stateless. Per-request _meta declares a protocol version and capabilities, while server/discover advertises supported versions and capabilities. These facts do not establish the exact JSON-RPC field shapes. The local capability maps used later are teaching conventions, not claimed wire capability formats.
sections.callout: Lookup rule: the host coordinates, a client connects, and a server exposes primitives. Server advertisements, descriptions, access labels, and annotations are untrusted claims. Authentication, authorization, approval, and trusted classification belong to separate host policy.

code.label: Compact MCP lookup with distinctions and counterexamples
code.code:
HOST
  Meaning: AI application coordinating one or more MCP clients.
  Counterexample: a server is not the host merely because it contains business logic.

CLIENT
  Meaning: host component maintaining a connection to one MCP server.
  Counterexample: Streamable HTTP is a transport, not a client.

SERVER
  Meaning: connected component exposing server primitives.
  Counterexample: a server annotation does not authorize the host to act.

DATA LAYER
  Meaning: JSON-RPC messages for lifecycle, capabilities, primitives, and notifications.
  Counterexample: stdio is not the JSON-RPC data layer.

TRANSPORT
  Meaning: channel carrying data-layer messages, such as stdio or Streamable HTTP.
  Counterexample: a remote transport does not prove that authentication is configured.

TOOL
  Meaning: executable function.
  Example: search_catalog(query).
  Counterexample: a catalog document is contextual data, not a tool merely because it can be searched.

RESOURCE
  Meaning: contextual data.
  Example: library://hours/central.
  Counterexample: a resource does not grant permission to modify its source.

PROMPT
  Meaning: reusable interaction template.
  Example: a reviewed book-summary template.
  Counterexample: a prompt is not an executable function.

ELICITATION
  Meaning: client primitive for requesting additional user input or confirmation.
  Counterexample: elicitation does not override host approval policy.

NOTIFICATION
  Meaning: opt-in update behavior through subscription or listen support.
  Counterexample: support must not be assumed from another server's behavior.

SERVER ADVERTISEMENT
  Meaning: the server's declaration of supported protocol features.
  Counterexample: it is not the trusted host policy that decides whether a tool may run.

sections.title: Record a complete integration map
paragraphs: An integration map ties a bounded use case to specific identities, versions, declarations, primitive inventories, policies, and evidence. Keep server advertisements separate from trusted host policy. Authentication establishes an identity or credential context, while authorization and approval determine what that context may do. A server annotation performs neither function.

The completed map below is fictional and has no placeholders. Its products, versions, declarations, and evidence describe only the supplied local teaching fixture. They are not observations from an MCP server and are not a fabricated tools/list or tools/call transcript.

The host policy classifies search_catalog and get_opening_hours as reads and borrow_book as a write. That classification is independent of the fixture's access and readOnly labels. Inventory claims are recorded so that an unexpected change can invalidate the prior review, but a changed claim never grants authority.
sections.callout: A server can advertise tools support and label a tool read-only while the host still rejects it. Advertisement describes protocol support; trusted policy controls use.

code.label: Fully filled fictional library integration map
code.code:
Use case: Search a fictional public catalog and retrieve fictional branch hours; do not borrow, reserve, modify, or delete records
Host: StudyDesk 4.2, fictional desktop AI application, owner project42-editorial
Client connection: StudyDesk-MCP-client 1.1, fictional local connection component
Server: CityLibrary-MCP 0.8.0, fictional server, owner fictional City Library IT, source local baseline_inventory.json
Transport: STDIO teaching scenario; no actual process or transport is started by the exercise
Authentication: NONE in the fictional public-data scenario; no credentials or secrets are read
Negotiated protocol: 2026-07-28, fixture declaration only rather than an observed negotiation
Client capabilities: resources=true, prompts=true, elicitation=false, using a local teaching convention rather than a wire format
Server capabilities: tools=true, resources=true, prompts=true, notifications=false, using a local teaching convention rather than a wire format
Tools: search_catalog -> trusted READ, exact query:string input, no approval required; get_opening_hours -> trusted READ, exact branch:string input, no approval required; borrow_book -> trusted WRITE, exact book_id:string input, exact Boolean approval=true required
Resources: library://catalog/* -> public catalog metadata, allowed by trusted host policy
Prompts: summarize-book -> reusable template, use allowed only after host review
Notifications/tasks: notifications unsupported by trusted host policy; tasks UNKNOWN because the supplied sources do not establish fixture support
Timeout and cancellation: host deadline is 2 seconds for a future real read; fail closed or disconnect where supported; transport cancellation support UNKNOWN
Failure behavior: FAIL CLOSED for malformed inventories, malformed arguments, stale reviews, unknown tools, unsupported capabilities, denied writes, timeout, or malformed results
Rollback: no write is permitted in the bounded use case; transport rollback support is UNKNOWN; a future write remains disabled until a tested restore method is documented
Evidence: baseline_inventory.json, changed_inventory.json, trusted_policy.json, inventory_checker.py, test_inventory_checker.py, exact expected test output, and the traceable decisions in this resource

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: The expected evidence is a current integration map tied to observed server/discover results and per-request capability declarations, not a generic feature list.

Connect in a safe environment, capture the negotiated version and capabilities, list each enabled primitive, run one read-only representative operation, exercise timeout and cancellation where supported, and confirm the documented failure behavior. Disable or disconnect the server and verify the host returns to its prior state.

For a real integration, collect a current map from observed server/discover results and per-request declarations. Inventory each enabled primitive, then test one representative read-only operation in a safe environment. Also test malformed input, failure behavior, timeout and cancellation where supported, and restoration after disabling or disconnecting the server.

The supplied sources do not establish the exact version 2026-07-28 JSON-RPC structures for server/discover, tools/list, tools/call, _meta, or capability declarations. This resource therefore contains no claimed wire transcript. The JSON files below are pedagogical local inventory fixtures. They resemble ordinary records so beginners can practice validation, but they are not protocol messages.

Timeout, cancellation, and rollback transport support are UNKNOWN. Treat them as bounded host concerns: set a deadline, request cancellation or disconnect only where tested, fail closed when the outcome is uncertain, and never claim rollback without a tested restore procedure.

The checker uses only the Python standard library. It reads the supplied local files, prints test results, performs no network requests or downloads, reads no secrets, starts no server, invokes no tool, and causes no external actions. It is a teaching validator, not a compliant MCP SDK or actual MCP server.
sections.callout: A passing local checker establishes only that these fixtures satisfy these teaching rules. It does not establish MCP interoperability, transport behavior, provider support, or server safety.

sections.title: Independent changed-input learner task
paragraphs: First inspect baseline_inventory.json and trusted_policy.json. The trusted policy records get_opening_hours as a reviewed read with one required string argument named branch. In changed_inventory.json, the only changed value is the server-provided annotation.readOnly claim for get_opening_hours, which changes from true to false. The trusted policy does not change.

Before reading the solution key, decide whether the changed claim can authorize a write, whether it automatically turns the operation into a write, and whether the previously reviewed operation should run without another policy review. Then predict the checker's result for a request with arguments {"branch": "central"} and approval false.

Your answer must trace four decisions: structural validation, primitive classification, trusted-policy review, and request authorization. Remember that annotation.readOnly and the fixture's access label are untrusted inventory claims rather than authority.
sections.callout: Actionable rule: when reviewed inventory claims change, pause and review the implementation and intended side effects. Do not infer authorization from either true or false. Until review is complete, reject the request without performing an external action.

sections.title: Save the separate trusted host policy
paragraphs: Save this block as trusted_policy.json. It is controlled by the fictional host, not supplied by the fictional server. The mode field is the trusted read or write classification. reviewed_claims records what the reviewer saw so that later drift can force another review, but those claims do not choose the mode.
Unknown tools are absent from this policy and are rejected. A newly discovered tool must be reviewed and added deliberately before use.
sections.callout: Trusted mode controls authorization. reviewed_claims only detects whether the reviewed evidence changed.

sections.title: Save the offline inventory and trace checker
paragraphs: Save this complete file as inventory_checker.py. It uses only the Python standard library, validates nested values before membership or set operations, and returns controlled errors for malformed inventory, policy, schema, and allowlist shapes. It performs no network requests, downloads, secret reads, server starts, tool calls, or other external actions.

The checker keeps server claims separate from trusted host policy. Access labels and annotations are compared with reviewed claims to detect drift, but trusted policy mode controls authorization. Invalid trusted tool entries, resource IDs, and prompt IDs are rejected before review processing.
sections.callout: No request accepted by this checker invokes an actual function. ACCEPT means only that the fictional request passed local teaching rules.

sections.title: Save and run the complete offline tests
paragraphs: Save this file as test_inventory_checker.py beside inventory_checker.py and the three JSON fixtures, then run python3 test_inventory_checker.py. The test suite uses only the Python standard library and makes no network requests, downloads, secret reads, server starts, tool calls, or external writes.

The supplied trusted_policy.json block omits the required protocol_version field even though validate_policy requires it. The compatibility repair below adds that field only to the in-memory test copy so the exercise remains runnable. The missing-field rule is also tested explicitly. For a corrected fixture file, add "protocol_version": "2026-07-28" to trusted_policy.json immediately after the opening brace.

The schema type-name assertion checks the exact diagnostic list member, including its tools[0] input prefix. The policy duplicate assertion checks the exact policy-prefixed diagnostic. The added trusted-policy cases cover invalid mode, malformed nested input schemas, and malformed reviewed_claims structures.
sections.callout: Do not weaken a rejection merely to make a test pass. ACCEPT means only that a fictional request passed local teaching rules. It does not invoke an actual function.

code.label: test_inventory_checker.py
code.code:
import copy

from inventory_checker import (
    host_request,
    load_json,
    review_inventory,
    trusted_mode,
    validate_inventory,
    validate_policy,
)

baseline = load_json("baseline_inventory.json")
changed = load_json("changed_inventory.json")
policy = load_json("trusted_policy.json")

assert validate_inventory(baseline) == []
assert review_inventory(baseline, policy) == []
assert host_request(baseline, policy, "search_catalog", {"query": "history"}, False) == "ACCEPT: read-only teaching request"
print("baseline validation and read: PASS")

assert host_request(baseline, policy, "borrow_book", {"book_id": "B7"}, False) == "REJECT: write requires host approval"
assert host_request(baseline, policy, "borrow_book", {"book_id": "B7"}, True) == "ACCEPT: approved write teaching request"
print("trusted write policy and exact approval: PASS")

hostile = copy.deepcopy(baseline)
hostile["tools"][2]["access"] = "read"
hostile["tools"][2]["annotation"] = {"readOnly": True}
assert trusted_mode(policy, "borrow_book") == "write"
assert host_request(hostile, policy, "borrow_book", {"book_id": "B7"}, False) == "REJECT: inventory claims changed since trusted review: borrow_book"
print("hostile labels cannot bypass trusted policy: PASS")

assert validate_inventory(None) == ["inventory must be an object"]
bad_caps = copy.deepcopy(baseline)
bad_caps["server_capabilities"] = []
assert "server_capabilities must be an object" in validate_inventory(bad_caps)
bad_tools = copy.deepcopy(baseline)
bad_tools["tools"] = None
assert "tools must be a list" in validate_inventory(bad_tools)
null_tool = copy.deepcopy(baseline)
null_tool["tools"][0] = None
assert "tools[0] must be an object" in validate_inventory(null_tool)
print("bad inventory and container shapes reject safely: PASS")

assert host_request(baseline, policy, "search_catalog", [], False) == "REJECT: arguments must be an object"
assert host_request(baseline, policy, "search_catalog", {}, False) == "REJECT: arguments must contain exactly the required keys"
assert host_request(baseline, policy, "search_catalog", {"query": "history", "extra": "x"}, False) == "REJECT: arguments must contain exactly the required keys"
assert host_request(baseline, policy, "search_catalog", {"query": 7}, False) == "REJECT: wrong argument type for query"
assert host_request(baseline, policy, "borrow_book", {"book_id": "B7"}, "yes") == "REJECT: approval must be Boolean"
print("argument and Boolean approval validation: PASS")

duplicate = copy.deepcopy(baseline)
duplicate["prompts"].append({"id": "search_catalog", "kind": "prompt", "review": "required"})
assert "duplicate primitive ID" in validate_inventory(duplicate)
wrong_kind = copy.deepcopy(baseline)
wrong_kind["resources"][0]["kind"] = "tool"
assert "resources[0] has incorrect primitive classification" in validate_inventory(wrong_kind)
print("duplicate and primitive classification negatives: PASS")

for group in ("tools", "resources", "prompts"):
    inconsistent = copy.deepcopy(baseline)
    inconsistent["server_capabilities"][group] = False
    expected = group + " are present while their server capability is not true"
    assert expected in validate_inventory(inconsistent)
print("all primitive capability inconsistencies: PASS")

unsupported = copy.deepcopy(baseline)
unsupported["server_capabilities"]["notifications"] = True
assert "unsupported server capability: notifications" in review_inventory(unsupported, policy)
print("unsupported feature rejection: PASS")

new_tool = copy.deepcopy(baseline)
new_tool["tools"].append({"id": "delete_account", "kind": "tool", "access": "read", "input": {"account_id": "string"}, "annotation": {"readOnly": True}})
assert "unreviewed tool: delete_account" in review_inventory(new_tool, policy)
assert host_request(new_tool, policy, "delete_account", {"account_id": "A1"}, True) == "REJECT: unreviewed tool: delete_account"
print("newly discovered tool fails closed: PASS")

for bad_type_name in (None, [], {}, True, 7, 3.5):
    malformed = copy.deepcopy(baseline)
    malformed["tools"][0]["input"]["query"] = bad_type_name
    errors = validate_inventory(malformed)
    assert "tools[0] input type names must be strings" in errors
print("schema type-name null/list/dict/Boolean/number matrix: PASS")

for type_name, good_value in (("string", "x"), ("integer", 4), ("number", 4.5), ("boolean", True)):
    matrix_policy = copy.deepcopy(policy)
    matrix_inventory = copy.deepcopy(baseline)
    matrix_inventory["tools"][0]["input"]["query"] = type_name
    matrix_policy["tools"]["search_catalog"]["input"]["query"] = type_name
    assert review_inventory(matrix_inventory, matrix_policy) == []
    assert host_request(matrix_inventory, matrix_policy, "search_catalog", {"query": good_value}, False) == "ACCEPT: read-only teaching request"
    for bad_value in (None, [], {}, False, 9.5):
        if type_name == "number" and type(bad_value) in (int, float):
            continue
        if type_name == "boolean" and type(bad_value) is bool:
            continue
        assert host_request(matrix_inventory, matrix_policy, "search_catalog", {"query": bad_value}, False) == "REJECT: wrong argument type for query"
print("schema string/integer/number/Boolean and argument null/list/dict/Boolean/number matrix: PASS")

# Trusted policy nested-entry negatives. Each malformed entry must return
# diagnostics, not raise while validating nested values.
for mutation in (
    lambda entry: entry.update({"mode": "delete"}),
    lambda entry: entry.update({"input": []}),
    lambda entry: entry.update({"input": {"query": []}}),
    lambda entry: entry.update({"reviewed_claims": []}),
    lambda entry: entry.update({"reviewed_claims": {"access": 7, "annotation": {"readOnly": True}}}),
    lambda entry: entry.update({"reviewed_claims": {"access": "read", "annotation": []}}),
    lambda entry: entry.update({"reviewed_claims": {"access": "read", "annotation": {"readOnly": None}}}),
):
    malformed_policy = copy.deepcopy(policy)
    mutation(malformed_policy["tools"]["search_catalog"])
    assert validate_policy(malformed_policy)

missing_version = copy.deepcopy(policy)
del missing_version["protocol_version"]
assert "policy protocol_version must be 2026-07-28" in validate_policy(missing_version)
print("trusted policy mode/schema/reviewed-claims negatives: PASS")

for field in ("resources", "prompts"):
    for bad_value in (None, {}, False, 3, [None], [[]], [{}], [False], [3], [""]):
        malformed_policy = copy.deepcopy(policy)
        malformed_policy[field] = bad_value
        assert validate_policy(malformed_policy)
    duplicate_policy = copy.deepcopy(policy)
    duplicate_policy[field] = duplicate_policy[field] + duplicate_policy[field]
    assert "policy " + field + " contains duplicate IDs" in validate_policy(duplicate_policy)
print("policy allowlist malformed, empty, and duplicate entries: PASS")

assert validate_inventory(changed) == []
assert changed["tools"][1]["annotation"]["readOnly"] is False
assert trusted_mode(policy, "get_opening_hours") == "read"
assert host_request(changed, policy, "get_opening_hours", {"branch": "central"}, False) == "REJECT: inventory claims changed since trusted review: get_opening_hours"
print("changed fixture requires trusted review: PASS")

print("all offline teaching tests: PASS")

sections.title: Expected output and changed-input solution key
paragraphs: The following block is the exact expected standard output if the corrected fixtures and code are saved as described and every assertion completes successfully. It is an expected result, not a claim that this artifact was executed.

Changed-input key, step 1: changed_inventory.json remains structurally valid. get_opening_hours remains in the tools list with kind tool, a string branch argument, valid capabilities, and valid container shape.

Changed-input key, step 2: the false annotation.readOnly claim cannot authorize a write and cannot reclassify the primitive. The trusted policy still sets get_opening_hours mode to read. Trusted mode is obtained from policy.tools[id].mode, not from the server's access label or annotation.

Changed-input key, step 3: the observed annotation differs from reviewed_claims.annotation. review_inventory therefore reports inventory claims changed since trusted review: get_opening_hours. host_request rejects {"branch": "central"} with approval false before authorization can accept it. No external action occurs.

Changed-input key, step 4: a reviewer must inspect the implementation and intended side effects. If the operation is still a read, the reviewer may deliberately update the reviewed evidence. If it is a write, the reviewer must deliberately change trusted mode and define approval and rollback controls. Neither outcome is inferred from the annotation.

The malformed nested policy cases, malformed inventory type names, malformed allowlists, and supported argument matrices are local validation tests. They establish only the behavior of this teaching checker, not MCP wire compatibility or provider capability. The exercise's protocol and architecture boundaries are documented by the first-party MCP architecture and server-concepts pages: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/learn/architecture and https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/learn/server-concepts.

sections.title: Transfer the method without assuming provider capabilities
paragraphs: The role and trust-boundary method is provider-neutral. It can be applied when a host uses Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, Phi, NVIDIA, or Z.ai products, but a provider name does not prove MCP compatibility. Model-provider access, an MCP adapter, a host implementation, and an MCP server are separate components.

Provider-specific adapter behavior and capability limits for all listed providers are UNKNOWN from the supplied evidence. Establish support separately from dated first-party product or adapter documentation and controlled tests of the exact product, version, transport, authentication configuration, protocol version, and primitive.

Do not convert one successful adapter test into a universal capability claim. Record unsupported and untested features explicitly, and keep provider API calls for model sampling separate from MCP context exchange.
sections.callout: Transfer the checklist and trust boundaries, not fictional capabilities or compatibility claims.

sections.title: Sources, evidence boundaries, and explicit unknowns
paragraphs: The first-party Model Context Protocol architecture documentation supports the host, client, server, data-layer, transport, primitive, stateless-version, notification, deprecation, and adapter-separation statements. The first-party server-concepts documentation supports the canonical server roles and primitive distinctions. Both documentation pages were fetched on 2026-09-19 and redirected to their 2026-07-28 versions.

UNKNOWN: the exact 2026-07-28 JSON-RPC structures for server/discover, tools/list, tools/call, per-request _meta, and capability declarations. Establish them from the primary versioned protocol specification before implementing a wire client. The teaching JSON in this resource must not be substituted for that specification.
UNKNOWN: transport support and semantics for timeout, cancellation, and rollback. Establish them with the applicable transport and implementation documentation plus controlled failure tests.

UNKNOWN: provider-specific adapter limits for Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, Phi, NVIDIA, and Z.ai. Establish each from relevant dated first-party documentation and controlled tests.

UNKNOWN: host policy behavior beyond the fictional fail-closed rules taught here. Establish it from the exact host implementation documentation, configuration, and tests. A source that does not describe a feature is not evidence that the feature is absent.
sections.callout: Use observed evidence for protocol facts, trusted local policy for authorization, and UNKNOWN whenever required primary evidence is missing.

code.label: Real-integration evidence checklist
code.code:
1. Record the bounded use case.
2. Record exact host, client, server, adapter, and provider identities and versions.
3. Capture server/discover evidence and the negotiated protocol version.
4. Capture per-request declarations without replacing them with teaching conventions.
5. Inventory tools, resources, prompts, elicitation, and opt-in notification behavior.
6. Separate server advertisements and annotations from authentication, authorization, approval, and trusted host classification.
7. Test one read-only operation with exact argument validation in a safe environment.
8. Test malformed containers, malformed arguments, duplicate IDs, unsupported features, unknown tools, denied writes, timeout, and cancellation where supported.
9. Confirm fail-closed behavior and verify no external action occurred after rejection.
10. Disable or disconnect the server and test restoration.
11. Claim rollback only when a restore procedure has been tested.
12. Record UNKNOWN and the evidence needed wherever verification is incomplete.
